name: Jeremy MacNeil (Brujah, Founder of the Free States)

system.concept: Anarchist Founder and De Facto Leader of the Anarch Free States
system.biography:
Background

Born in the Scottish highlands in 1631 and Embraced by a 7th-generation @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} after a skirmish against Cromwell's forces, Jeremy MacNeil fought for Irish freedom, then American independence, before @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} expansion pushed him ever westward to Los Angeles. When Don Sebastian's goons savagely beat him for defying the Prince, the resulting anarch outcry became the spark of the 1944 Revolt. Jeremy, Salvador Garcia, Crispus Attucks, and Marguerite Foccart led the uprising that destroyed Don Sebastian and founded the Anarch Free States, a stretch of California from the Mexican border to San Jose governed by no prince.

Roleplaying Hints

A committed anarchist, Jeremy has little interest in personally governing and strongly resists both his own accretion of power and any other Kindred's attempts to rule. He believes the strong proving themselves in a free society will eventually create genuine Kindred brotherhood. He reserved the San Fernando Valley and central Los Angeles as neutral, baron-free territory for himself and defended it with his coterie. He tolerates Smiling Jack's disruptive presence in the Free States out of reluctance to give the anarchs orders, though it worries him. Unknown to Jeremy, Christopher Houghton (a hidden @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} elder secretly infatuated with him) has been the true unseen power protecting the Free States since their founding.
system.notes: Haven: heavily guarded estate off Mulholland Drive in the Hollywood Hills, and a second haven beneath City Hall. Survived an @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} assassination contract from the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}'s Inner Circle in 1955 (with Crispus Attucks). Secretly the object of the ancient @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} Christopher Houghton's infatuation and protection.

system.description: You focus your preternatural speed into the smallest of motions, allowing feats of fine manipulation beyond mortal (or even ordinary Cainite) capability, such as micro-precise crafting or delicate surgery. Spend two Blood Traits and a Willpower Trait, then spend five minutes in a trance-like state of concentration. For the next five minutes you gain two free retests on all challenges related to precision, fine manipulation, or moving something without disturbing its surroundings. Any actions that do not involve fine manipulation require you to bid an additional Trait, and you lose all ties on any challenge involving gross physical movement, including combat.

Calling upon her preternatural speed, a Kindred using this power appears to undertake several actions at once, “flickering” from one action to the next. This is particularly useful in combat, as one's foe cannot guess which of the actions he perceives is the one with which the character follows through. The character seems to be a dervish while this power is in effect, beginning countless feints, dodges and parries.

System: The player spends a Blood Trait to activate this power. For the turn in which the character calls upon this power, she may use six additional Physical Traits (Graceful x2, Nimble x2, Quick x2) for the purposes of defense. These bonus Traits do not apply to the character's attacks. She also gains a single “Stutter” retest in any challenge, applicable for defensive actions. The Stutter retest is always the last retest declared in a challenge, unless the attacker declares the use of Might.

Facetiously named, this power allows the Kindred to physically knock another character away from herself with the slightest of touches. Although this power does no damage in and of itself, its use is quite humbling — to be hurled away from an elder in a social setting has its embarrassing repercussions. Some Kindred use this power surreptitiously, touching their victims and sending them reeling across the room; others use it as a not-so-subtle display of their might, giving their victim a casual slap with overwhelming results.

System: The player spends a Blood Trait and must succeed in a physical challenge to touch the target (this may be done surreptitiously, but the player may not make use of other Potence benefits). The challenge is not required if the subject allows the player to touch him (a handshake, a “friendly” hand on the shoulder, etc). This power hurls the victim 20 feet directly away from the invoking character. If the subject strikes a wall or other solid obstacle, he suffers two health levels of bashing damage. Otherwise, the character needs to win a static physical challenge against six Traits to remain standing.

With this power, the Kindred becomes capable of truly impressive physical displays. He may leap from rooftop to rooftop over entire streets, jump to a fire escape a dozen feet over his head, and perform other feats of athleticism. This is useful both for pursuit and evasion, but is quite a breach of the Masquerade should anyone see this power in use.

System: The player may use this power to allow her character to leap up to 25 feet vertically or 40 feet horizontally. She must succeed in a static physical challenge against four Traits (retest with Athletics) to land correctly — if she fails the challenge, the Storyteller should assess results as appropriate.

items.name: Presence — 2 Intermediate — Command the Wary Steed

system.description:
Through use of this power the Cainite can cause enemies' mounts to rear and bolt, singly or en masse, by the strength of his gaze alone, or bolster the courage and tractability of allied steeds for greater control in battle.

System: The player spends a Willpower point and rolls Manipulation + Animal Ken (difficulty 7). Enemy mounts become terrified and nigh uncontrollable: Ride roll difficulties increase by three and mounted combat becomes impossible. Friendly mounts become far more pliant (-2 difficulty on all Ride rolls) and may be coerced into situations they would normally avoid.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book Three: Zealots

system.description: By winning a Social Challenge, you render the target favorably disposed toward you for the rest of the scene or an hour, unable to insult or attack you unless you act against them first.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines
